parole.significato: wave (on the surface of a liquid)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *alto, borrowed from Proto-Norse, from Proto-Germanic *aldǭ, whence also allas and Old Norse alda (“wave”). Cognate with Ingrian alto, Ludian aldo, Veps ald.
From Proto-Finnic *apaja (compare Ingrian apaja, Votic apajõ), borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*abjō) or earlier Proto-Germanic *abjǭ (compare dialectal Swedish ävja, Old Norse efja).
From Proto-Finnic *arina, borrowed from Proto-Norse ᚨᛉᛁᚾᚨᛉ (aʀinaʀ).
From Proto-Finnic *arkku, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚨᚱᚲᚢ (*arku) (compare Proto-Germanic *arkō and Old Norse ǫrk), from Latin arca.
From Proto-Finnic *eineh, probably borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚨᚠᚾᛁᛃᚨ (*afnija). Related to Estonian eine.
From Proto-Finnic *elki, probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse illr).
From Proto-Finnic *haasja, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (whence Norwegian Nynorsk hesje and Swedish hässja).

parole.significato: wound, sore (injury, such as a cut, stab, or tear)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *haava (compare Estonian haav), borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*hawwa-/*hagwa-) (compare Swedish hugg), from Proto-Germanic *hawwą (“blow, hit”) (compare Proto-Germanic *hawwaną).

parole.significato: shoulder (joint between the arm and the torso)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hartija, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Icelandic herðar and Faroese herðar (“shoulders”)), from Proto-Germanic *hardį̄ (“shoulder”). Compare Karelian hartie.

parole.significato: The mesh fabric of a fishnet or fish-trap.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *habas, borrowed from early Proto-Norse [script needed] (*hābaz) (later *ᚺᚨᛒᚨᛉ (*hābaʀ)), from Proto-Germanic *hēbaz. Doublet of haavi.
From Proto-Finnic *humala, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*humalā) (compare Swedish humle), itself probably borrowed from Proto-Slavic *xъmelь.

parole.significato: felt (matted, non-woven material of wool or other fibre)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *hoopa, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚦᛟᛒᛟ (*þōbō), from Proto-Germanic *þōbô, whence Old Norse þófi (“felt”). Cognate with Ingrian hoopa, Karelian huopa, Veps hob.
From Proto-Finnic *hoora, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *hōrǭ (“whore, adultress”).
From Proto-Finnic *joulu, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛃᛖᚢᛚᚢ (*jeulu). Doublet of juhla.

parole.significato: a rope used to draw a sledge or toboggan
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *juko, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Norwegian oke (“crossbeam”)).
From Proto-Finnic *juusto (compare Estonian juust), borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*jūstaʀ) (compare Swedish ost) or Proto-Germanic *justaz.

parole.significato: a wooden log (often a debarked one) laid under something for transportation, e.g. laid diagonally while building a log…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kalju, possibly borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?].
From Proto-Finnic *kammijo, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*skammijǭ), from Proto-Germanic *skammijǭ (“little house”). Compare Icelandic skemma (“a storehouse”).

parole.significato: rock (mass of stone projecting out of water or just underwater)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kari (compare Estonian kari), borrowed from late Proto-Norse [script needed] (*skarj(a)-) (compare Swedish skär, English skerry), from Proto-Germanic *skarją.
From Proto-Finnic *kasa, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Swedish kasi, Swedish kase (“heap, collection of something”), Old Norse kǫs (“heap, pile”)), from Proto-Germanic *kasō.

parole.significato: trade, commerce, buying and selling, trading, dealing, business, traffic
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *kauppa, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse kaupa, Old English ċēap and German Kauf), which in turn from Latin caupo.
From Proto-Finnic *kirnu, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *kirnijǭ (“churn”).

parole.significato: snout, muzzle (protruding part of an animal's head which includes the nose, mouth and jaws)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *koono (compare Estonian koon, Votic koono), likely borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚷᛟᚾᛟ (*gōnō).
From Proto-Finnic *kurkku (compare Estonian, Livonian, and Veps kurk), borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*kwerku), from Proto-Germanic *kwerkō (compare Old Norse kverk, Swedish Kvarken).
From Proto-Finnic *laaka, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*lāgaʀ).

From Proto-Finnic *lahja, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛒᛚᚨᚺᛃᛟ (*blahjo), from Proto-Germanic *blahjōn (“sheet, cloth”) (compare Icelandic blæja (“veil”)). Cognates include Votic lahjõ (“wedding gift”) and Ingrian lahja (“gift”).
From Proto-Finnic *laidun, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*laidu).

parole.significato: barn, hovel, hayshed (unheated, inexpensively built roofed storage for agricultural equipment or products, especially h…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lato (compare Estonian ladu), borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚺᛚᚨᚦᛟ (*hlaþō) (compare Old Norse hlaða, Swedish lada).
From Proto-Finnic *lattija, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚠᛚᚨᛏᛃᚨ (*flatja), from Proto-Germanic *flatją. Compare Karelian late.
From Proto-Finnic *liikkijo, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *flikkiją.

parole.significato: A large number; slew, flock, swarm.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *liuta, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛚᛖᚢᛞᚨ- (*leuda-), from Proto-Germanic *liudīz (“people”).

parole.significato: lock (a mechanism used to lock, or fasten such that a key is required to unfasten)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *lukko, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *lukǭ (compare *luką (“lock”) and English lock). Cognate to Ingrian lukku, Karelian lukku, Ludian lukk, Estonian lukk, Veps lukol, Votic lukku.

From Proto-Finnic *lupa (compare Estonian luba), borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] or earlier Proto-Germanic *lubą (“praise”) (compare Old Norse lof (“praise, permission”), Swedish lov (“permission; praise”)). Attested since the time of Mikael Agricola (output c. 1543–1552).

parole.significato: belly, stomach (abdomen, especially a round one)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *maha (compare Karelian maha, Ludian maha, Votic maha), probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Proto-Germanic *magô, Swedish mage).

parole.significato: saltbush, orach (plant of the genus Atriplex)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *malcca (compare Estonian malts), borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Danish mælde), from Proto-Germanic *meldǭ (compare German Melde).

parole.significato: tack, thumbtack, pin, pushpin, drawing pin (a small nail-like fastener that can be pushed in with one's finger)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nasta, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Norwegian neste, Old English nestila, Old Gutnish nast).

parole.significato: cattle; cow, bull (animal of the species Bos taurus, regardless of gender or age)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nauta, borrowed from Proto-Norse ᚾᚨᚢᛏᚨ (nauta) (compare Old Norse naut, Swedish nöt (“cattle”)), from Proto-Germanic *nautą.
From Proto-Finnic *nopëda (compare Estonian nobe), possibly borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*snōƀ(r)jaR).
From Proto-Finnic *noora, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛊᚾᛟᚱᚨ (*snōra).

parole.significato: to fuck, to screw, to have sexual intercourse with
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *nussidak (compare Estonian nussima, Karelian nussie, Livonian nuššõ, Võro nus'ma, Votic nussia), possibly a borrowing from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Danish nusse, nosse).

parole.significato: beer, ale (fermented beverage made of malt, originally barley, but also other cereals are used)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *olut, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*ǫluþ-) (compare Swedish öl). Possibly akin to kalja, if it is an early borrowing from an Indo-European language.
From Proto-Finnic *piitta (compare Estonian piit, Livonian pīţ, Votic piittõ), borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse biti).

parole.significato: to spoil, ruin, blight, destroy (to cause the ruin of)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pilat'ak (compare Karelian pilata, Votic pilatõ), possibly borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse bila (“to fail”)).
From Proto-Finnic *porkka, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*forkaʀ) (compare Old Norse forkr), from Proto-Germanic *furkaz.
From Proto-Finnic *raato (compare Ingrian raato, Karelian roato), borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*brāđō) (compare Swedish bråd (“piece of meat”)), from Proto-Germanic *brēdô.

parole.significato: sober (that does not drink alcohol; not given to excessive drinking of alcohol)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rait'is, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *raidi(ja)z.

parole.significato: the main road of a village that goes down the middle of it; a lone village road splitting the village in half
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raitti (compare Karelian reitti, Veps rait, Votic raitti), borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Swedish vret).

parole.significato: synonym of takaraivo (“back of the head”)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raivo, by metathesis from earlier *rawjo, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *trawją (“bowl, vessel”) (compare English tray).

parole.significato: unburned swidden; a forest that has been cleared for slash and burn but has not yet been burnt
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rasi, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*grasja), from Proto-Germanic *grasą.

parole.significato: ruin (remains of destroyed or dilapidated construction)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *raunijo, possibly equivalent to rauna + -io, derived from a borrowing from Proto-Norse [Term?] (compare Old Norse hraun). Related to Ingrian raunio, Karelian raunivo and Votic raunio.

parole.significato: reef (chain or range of rocks, sand, or coral lying at or near the surface of the water)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *riutta, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚷᚱᛖᚢᛏᚨ (*greuta), from Proto-Germanic *greutą (“grit, gravel, sand”), compare with Old Norse grjót (“coarse stones, rubble”).
From Proto-Finnic *räivä, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *hraiwą.

From Proto-Finnic *saatto (cognates include Estonian saad, Karelian soatto, Veps sat and Votic saatto), borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*sātō), from Proto-Germanic *sētǭ (compare Icelandic sáta).

From Proto-Finnic *sukka, borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *sukkaz (“sock”) (compare English sock, Swedish socka), from Latin soccus. Finnic cognates include Ingrian sukka, Karelian sukka, Karelian šukka, Livvi sukku, Ludian suk, Estonian sukk, Livonian sukā and Votic sukkõ.

parole.significato: burden (heavy load; (figuratively) cause of worry, anxiety, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *taakka, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᛊᛏᚨᚲᚲᚨᛉ (*stakkaʀ), from Proto-Germanic *stakkaz (compare Old Norse stakkr (“hay stack, heap”)). Doublet of takka.

From Proto-Finnic *tanhu- (compare Estonian tänav, Ingrian tanvas, Karelian tanhut, Veps tannaz, Votic tanava (Kattila)), borrowed from Proto-Norse ᛏᚨᚾᚺᚢ- (*tanhu-), from Proto-Germanic *tanhwą (compare Old Norse tá (“path”)).

parole.significato: disease (abnormal condition of the body causing discomfort or dysfunction)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tauti, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*dauđi) (cf. Proto-Germanic *dauþuz). Cognates include Estonian taud (“a pestilence or infectious disease”), Icelandic dauði (“death”) and Swedish död (“death”).

parole.significato: plug (any piece of wood, metal, or other substance used to stop or fill a hole)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tulppa, probably borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*stulpā), from Proto-Germanic *stulpô. Doublet of tolppa.
From Proto-Finnic *vainijo, borrowed from Proto-Norse [script needed] (*hwainiō), from Proto-Germanic *hwainō (compare English whin, Old Norse hvein and Swedish ven). Cognate with Estonian vain.
From Proto-Finnic *varjëldak, equivalent to varj- + -ella, with a root borrowed from Proto-Norse [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *warjaną.
From Proto-Finnic *viikko, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚹᛁᚲᛟ (*wiko) (compare Swedish vecka, Old Norse vika and Icelandic vika), from Proto-Germanic *wikǭ (“week”).

parole.significato: sign (such as a road sign; clearly visible object, generally flat, bearing a short message in words or pictures; especi…
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *viitta, borrowed from Proto-Norse *ᚹᛁᛏᚨ (*wīta) (compare Icelandic viti (“sign, omen”)), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *wītaną.
